items.stem: What does Spring Boot auto-configuration actually do?

options.text: It configures beans automatically based on the classpath and properties, which you can override
options.rationale: Correct: auto-configuration wires sensible defaults from the classpath/properties and is overridable.

options.text: It writes your business logic for you
options.rationale: Auto-configuration wires infrastructure, not business logic.

options.text: It prevents you from defining your own beans
options.rationale: Your explicit beans override auto-configured ones.

options.text: It only works without any dependencies on the classpath
options.rationale: It reacts to what is on the classpath; dependencies are what trigger it.

items.explanation: Correct: auto-configuration wires sensible defaults from the classpath/properties and is overridable.

items.stem: Select TWO practices for a well-behaved Spring Boot REST endpoint.

options.text: Validate the request body and return 400 for invalid input
options.rationale: Correct: validating input and returning 400 communicates client errors clearly.

options.text: Return status codes that reflect the outcome (e.g. 201 on create, 404 when missing)
options.rationale: Correct: meaningful status codes are part of a correct REST API.

options.text: Return 200 OK for every response including errors
Put database credentials directly in the controller code
options.rationale: Secrets belong in externalized configuration, not source.

options.text: Swallow all exceptions and return an empty body
options.rationale: Silently swallowing errors hides failures from clients.

items.explanation: Correct: validating input and returning 400 communicates client errors clearly.

items.stem: How should environment-specific settings (like a database URL) be handled in Spring Boot?

options.text: Externalize them via configuration and profiles per environment
options.rationale: Correct: externalized config with profiles keeps environment values out of code.

options.text: Hard-code them in the Java source
options.rationale: Hard-coding couples the build to one environment and leaks values.

options.text: Store them in the compiled class names
options.rationale: Class names are not a configuration mechanism.

options.text: Ask the user to type them on every request
options.rationale: Infrastructure settings are not per-request user input.

items.explanation: Correct: externalized config with profiles keeps environment values out of code.
